scope:
Stage S3R design review of 009-asking-to-agree at 85447a7 (no diff; nothing built). One reviewer, three lenses in order: spec-compliance, security, architecture. The schema has one top-level lens and no per-finding lens field, so each finding's id prefix carries its lens: SPEC = spec-compliance, SEC = security, ARCH = architecture. READ: spec.md, sketch.md, plan.md, research.md, tasks.md, decisions.md, planning-notes.md, CONSTITUTION.md, CONTEXT.md (glossary terms), docs/contributing/standards/testing.md, mvp_compliance/models.py (40-240, 348-505, 740-1087), views.py, urls.py, both templates, agreement.js, tests/test_views.py (outline, TestPageStrings 875-934, TestTemplateOverride 788-811), tests/settings.py, tests/urls*.py, tests/conftest.py, demo/urls.py, demo/views.py. tests/test_models.py was outlined only. Resolved packages: Django 6.1.1 and django-mvp 0.25.1 in .venv. PROBED by running, in an in-memory SQLite database with tests.settings, no file written: bulk_create(ignore_conflicts=True) through the manager, the outstanding_for().in_force() chain, url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme over 43 inputs, and path variants of the fixed route agreed/. PostgreSQL was not run: CI and tests are SQLite only. Templates and agreement.js were read for the context they need, not reviewed. D14 and D16 were taken as settled. 

Q1 (record_many against record()). Confirmed: Acceptance.objects.bulk_create reaches AcceptanceQuerySet.bulk_create (models.py:772-795), which runs only refuse_if_notice and then Django's insert; five versions with one already accepted cost 2 queries (the notice SELECT, one INSERT OR IGNORE), wrote 4, left the existing row's accepted_at unchanged. What bulk_create skips that record() does (models.py:872-920, plus Acceptance.save 1054-1061 which record() reaches through get_or_create): (a) the is_published check, models.py:894: probed, bulk_create writes an acceptance of a draft. plan.md:82 restores it and T002 tests it. Covered. (b) subject_of, models.py:911 and 1004-1028: bulk_create writes whatever subject it is given. plan.md:83-84 says 'the same subject record() would write' and T002 asserts the subject. Covered, provided the implementer calls Acceptance.subject_of and not str(user.pk); the unsaved-user RecordError has no planned test and the view cannot produce one. (c) the immutability refusal in save(), models.py:1056-1059: not run, and not needed, because an INSERT with ignore_conflicts cannot alter a stored row and a primary-key collision is ignored too. Covered by T002's 'its record is unchanged'. (d) save()'s second notice check, models.py:1060: replaced by the queryset's own, models.py:793-794. Probed: a notice in the batch raises RecordError and writes nothing. Covered by T002. (e) the IP address rule, models.py:903-910: plan.md:83-84 and T002. Covered. (f) pre_save and post_save: not sent (.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/django/db/models/query.py:845). The package has no receiver (only signals.py:9 version_published). A host project's receiver on Acceptance is not covered and not documented: ARCH-001. (g) get_or_create's race handling (.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/django/db/models/query.py:1075-1078): replaced by the unique constraint, models.py:992-997. Covered. Other side of ignore_conflicts, probed: on SQLite INSERT OR IGNORE also drops a row that breaks NOT NULL, silently (a row with accepted_at=None raised nothing and wrote nothing). That is a failed write with no error, which plan.md step 4's second read exists to catch, so FR-008 is doing real work. Oracle has supports_ignore_conflicts False: ARCH-001. 

Q2 (FR-005). A submitted 'agree' value cannot name its way to a record: plan.md:104-105 selects from the entries read for request.user in that request, so a superseded id, a draft id, another person's or an already-accepted document's id match nothing, and T004 scenario 9 tests three of those. A version replaced, a document first published, accepted elsewhere or made a notice between the GET and the POST are all settled by that first read (T009 scenarios 6 and 7). Between get_entries() and the write inside one request there is no lock, and three things can happen, each in a window of milliseconds: (1) a new version is published: probed, the loaded instance still says status=current and bulk_create records an acceptance of the now superseded version. The second read keeps the person on the page. FR-005 is breached to the letter, and the record can never be removed. (2) the document is made a notice before refuse_if_notice: RecordError, the whole batch fails and the page says nothing was recorded, where FR-013 says pass over. research.md:56-58 accepts this. (3) it is made a notice between refuse_if_notice and the INSERT: an acceptance of a notice is written. record() has the same gap today. All three are SPEC-002, low. A hand-built POST naming the id of a current, outstanding version the person's page never listed is recorded: the server keeps no memory of what it listed, and the 'listed' field is the client's own. Only the person themselves can send it (CSRF), so it is not raised as a finding. 

Q3 (FR-008, FR-012, coverage). plan.md steps 3 to 5 record the partial agreement and render again with 'missing'; that is FR-012 and US-3 scenario 3 as written (T009), and FR-008 is the second read (T007 scenario 5). No scenario in spec.md is undemonstrated. FR against tasks: 26 of 26. FR-001 T004; 002 T004; 003 T009; 004 T002+T004; 005 T004+T009; 006 T004; 007 T004; 008 T007; 009 T007; 010 T007; 011 T007 (see SPEC-003); 012 T009; 013 T009; 014 T009; 015 T011+T004; 016 T011; 017 T011; 018 T011; 019 T004; 020 T013; 021 T013; 022 T013; 023 T002+T009; 024 T004 (nothing agreed records nothing) + T006 docs, and nothing in the plan intercepts another address; 025 T001+T006; 026 T006+T008+T012+T014, all five topics placed. SC against tasks: 9 of 9. SC-001 T004+T007+T009; 002 T007; 003 T004; 004 T009; 005 T007+T011; 006 T011; 007 T011; 008 T013; 009 T009. Acceptance scenarios: US-1 9 of 9 (T004), US-2 6 of 6 (T007), US-3 7 of 7 (T009), US-4 8 of 8 (T011, scenario 8 by T012's docs), US-5 4 of 4 (T013). Edge cases with no planned test: a POST after the session ended (LoginRequiredMixin.dispatch covers every method, .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/django/contrib/auth/mixins.py:71-72) and a staff user. Neither is an acceptance scenario. Tasks with no FR behind them: is_optional, the optional rows and DemoAgreementView (D16, taken as settled). 

Q4 (get_destination). Probed against .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/django/utils/http.py:274-334 with allowed_hosts={'testserver'}. LEAVES THE SITE: nothing found. Refused: another host, //host, /\\host, \\\\host, http:///host, https:host, javascript:, a tab inside or before the slashes, user@host, host\\@site, another port, an upper-case host, ftp. Let through and still on the site: 'evil.example' as a bare word (a relative path), '/%2F/evil.example', '/%5Cevil.example'. One gap: 'http://testserver/x' passes on an https page because plan.md:116-118 does not pass require_https, where Django's own sign-in does (.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/django/contrib/auth/views.py:54-58): ARCH-002. LOOPS BACK TO THE PAGE while differing from the page's own path as a string: '/legal/agree' with no trailing slash (probed on agreed/: 301 from APPEND_SLASH to the page), '/legal/%61gree/' (probed: answered by the page's route), '/legal/x/../agree/' and '/legal/./agree/' (a browser normalises them), the relative forms '.', './', '../agree/', '?next=/x/', '?', '#x', and '/legal/agree/ ' with trailing space. Caught only if the comparison parses the path out first: 'http://testserver/legal/agree/', 'https://testserver/legal/agree/', '//testserver/legal/agree/', '/legal/agree/?next=/x/', '/legal/agree/#top'. Not the page: '/legal//agree/' and '/legal/agree/;x' (404), 'agree/' (resolves to /legal/agree/agree/, 404). Indirect: '/account/login/?next=/legal/agree/'. In the package as planned each of these costs one extra trip through the page and ends at the default, because the page redirects when nothing is outstanding and a nested next is finite. SEC-002. The setting's own value is the project's: resolve_url returns a URL as given (.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/django/shortcuts.py:173-208), including another site or the page itself, and raises NoReverseMatch for a bare word that names no route. 

Q5 (change detectors, wording, appearance). One: T009's 'required entries come before optional ones' pins a choice sketch.md:116-119 lists as open to change (SPEC-004). Nothing else: 'missing', 'failed' and 'changed' are asserted as context flags, not sentences; the forbidden-word sweep (T006) is the Article XIII contract and follows TestAgreedDocumentsStrings; the form id, data-required and the script tag are hooks testing.md section 1 lists as tested; aria-describedby is checked against an element that exists, not against wording; query counts are compared at one and ten, never pinned; escaping and link targets are behaviour. No planned test asserts a badge variant, alignment or a class. 

ROUTES (security lens): one added, agree/ under the package's include, GET and POST, LoginRequiredMixin on dispatch, every query narrowed to request.user, nothing in the address or the form names another person. The demo adds legal/agree/ to a subclass, demo only. No admin, router or signal registration. OTHER SIDES CHECKED: the reserved slug is refused by full_clean and the admin (T013) and not by Document.objects.create(), which T013 covers through the route order; a document already published under 'agree' cannot be renamed (models.py:65-77, 197-217), which T014's CHANGELOG line states. A project that mounts the package's pages without django-mvp's was not traced for this page. Verdict approve: no verified critical or high finding. One medium (SPEC-001) is a ruling for the maintainer, not a plan edit.

findings.claim: [spec-compliance] The line under the title tells every person 'You will not be able to use the app without agreeing to all required documents', and this feature stops nobody. In the package as shipped every outstanding document is required (is_optional returns False), so every install shows the sentence on every visit, and no route keeps the promise until #87 exists. The fault is between the approved sketch and the approved spec, not in the plan.
findings.evidence: sketch.md:108-110 rules the sentence and sketch.md:94 says the build may not undo it. spec.md:325-326 (FR-024) and spec.md:37-40: 'This feature stops nobody. It is a page a person is sent to, or opens, and can leave like any other page.' decisions.md D1 says the same. plan.md:123 carries the subtitle into the view 'as approved' and plan.md:125-126 restates that the view never stops a request. agreement.html:30 renders page.subtitle; agreement.html:17 and outstanding.html:17 repeat 'required'.
findings.suggested_fix: No plan edit. Put the question to the maintainer before T005 writes the string: keep the sentence as ruled, knowing it is untrue until #87, or re-rule the wording. Record the answer in decisions.md. Whichever is chosen, the subtitle is one lazy string in the view and no test asserts it.

findings.claim: [security] US-1 ends with an open redirect. T005 builds 'a get_destination() that returns next or /', with no host check, and T004 asserts that agreeing redirects to next. The check arrives in T012, three stories later. The branch merges as one pull request, so no release carries it, but US-1 is the unit that is dispatched and reviewed, and for three stories /legal/agree/?next=https://other.example sends a signed-in person off the site after they agree.
findings.evidence: tasks.md:24 (T005) against tasks.md:45-46 (T011, T012) and plan.md:116-119. FR-016 and SC-007 (spec.md:307-308, 361). feature-state.json: one draft pull request, #88, for all five stories.
findings.suggested_fix: Move one clause, add nothing: T005's get_destination() keeps next only when url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme passes for the request's host, else '/'. Move 'a next on another host, with another scheme, or protocol-relative is replaced by the default' from T011 to T004. T012 keeps the setting, the page's-own-address rule and the redirect in get().

findings.claim: [security] 'Its path is not this page's own' is defeated by a next that reaches the page under another spelling. Each passes Django's host check and is not equal to the page's path as a string: no trailing slash, a percent-encoded letter, dot segments, and the relative forms '.', '?x=1' and '#x'. In the package as planned the cost is one extra trip through the page before the default (US-4 scenario 6 says 'not sent round again'). With a view whose is_optional answers true and only optional documents left, pressing Continue returns the person to the page every time.
findings.evidence: plan.md:116-119. T011 (tasks.md:45) tests only 'the page's own address, with or without a query string'. Probed with tests.settings: url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme returns True for '/legal/agree', '/legal/%61gree/', '/legal/x/../agree/', '.', '?next=/x/', '#x' (.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/django/utils/http.py:304-334). GET /legal/agreed answers 301 to /legal/agreed/ and GET /legal/%61greed/ is answered by the agreed route, so the same holds for agree/.
findings.reproduction: With the page built: signed in with nothing outstanding, GET /legal/agree/?next=/legal/agree (no trailing slash). Expected by US-4 scenario 6: one redirect to the default. Planned behaviour: redirect to /legal/agree, then 301 to /legal/agree/, then the default.
findings.suggested_fix: In plan.md get_destination(), compare after normalising and name it: strip the value, urljoin it onto the request's path, take urlsplit().path, unquote it, and treat it as the page when it equals request.path with trailing slashes ignored. In T011 extend the scenario 6 case to four inputs: no trailing slash, a percent-encoded letter, '.', and '?x=1'. No new mechanism and no resolver call.

findings.claim: [security] FR-019 rests on the host project having CsrfViewMiddleware installed. The plan names no protection of its own ('CSRF protection is Django's'), and the planned test passes because tests/settings.py installs the middleware. In a project without it, another site can submit the form for a signed-in person and an acceptance, which can never be deleted, is recorded in their name. Django guards its own sign-in view with csrf_protect for the same reason.
findings.evidence: plan.md:49 (Article V row) and tasks.md:23 (T004, Client(enforce_csrf_checks=True)). tests/settings.py:36 installs the middleware. .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/django/contrib/auth/views.py:27 imports csrf_protect for LoginView. .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/mvp/templates/cotton/form/index.html emits {% csrf_token %} for a post form, so the token is already on the page. Article XI: an acceptance is never deleted.
findings.suggested_fix: One line in plan.md's view section and in T005: AgreementView's dispatch is wrapped with method_decorator(csrf_protect). T004's existing CSRF test then holds whatever the project's middleware is. No new test.

findings.claim: [spec-compliance] Inside one request nothing holds the list still between get_entries() and the write, so FR-005 and FR-013 can each be missed in a window of milliseconds. A version published in that window is recorded although it is no longer current. A document made a notice in that window fails the whole batch and the person is told nothing was recorded. Neither sends anybody on wrongly, because the second read decides.
findings.evidence: plan.md:104-112 (steps 1, 3, 4) and plan.md:82-86. Probed: a Version instance loaded as current still reports status 'current' after another version of its document is published, and bulk_create(ignore_conflicts=True) wrote an acceptance of the superseded version. models.py:793-794 refuses a notice before the insert, not with it. research.md:56-58 already accepts the notice case. decisions.md D7 holds that an acceptance of a replaced version would be true and settles nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: No code. Add one sentence to research.md under 'Which errors are a failed write' and one entry in decisions.md: the list is not locked for the length of a request, a version replaced or a document made a notice in that window is not passed over, and the second read is what keeps the person on the page. Closing it would need a row lock that SQLite does not have, which no requirement here earns.

findings.claim: [spec-compliance] research.md's premise for FR-011 is true on one side only. A record on the logger mvp_compliance.views goes through the project's LOGGING, but under Django's default LOGGING only the 'django' logger has handlers, so the failure reaches standard error and never the ADMINS mail that the project's unhandled errors get. T007's assertion (an error on mvp_compliance.views with the exception attached) passes either way.
findings.evidence: research.md:62-64. .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/django/utils/log.py:55-59: handlers 'console' and 'mail_admins' sit on the 'django' logger and the root logger has none. spec.md:296-297 (FR-011): 'reported to the host project the way its other errors are'. tasks.md:32 (T008) plans to document 'the logger to attach error reporting to'.
findings.suggested_fix: Edit T008's documentation clause to say what the reader must be told: under Django's default LOGGING a failed write is written to standard error only, and a project that mails or forwards its errors attaches a handler to mvp_compliance.views. Correct the sentence at research.md:62-63 to match. No code change and no new test.

findings.claim: [spec-compliance] T009 plans a test that 'required entries come before optional ones'. No requirement asks for that order. It is a choice the sketch lists as open to change, and for a view with optional documents it departs from the name order FR-014 fixes. The test can only fail when somebody changes the arrangement on purpose.
findings.evidence: tasks.md:38 (T009, last clause). sketch.md:116-119: 'Choices made in building it, each open to change: ... Required documents come first, optional ones after.' spec.md:303-304 (FR-014). docs/contributing/standards/testing.md:16-18 and 35-36 ('the order of sections on a page').
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the clause 'required entries come before optional ones' from T009. Keep the sort in T010: it is what the approved screen shows. T009's name-order assertion (scenario 5, FR-014) stays and covers the package's own behaviour.

findings.claim: [architecture] record_many() differs from record() in two ways a consumer can observe, and neither is in the plan's documentation tasks. It sends no pre_save or post_save, so a project that listens for a new Acceptance hears nothing from the page. On a database without ignore_conflicts support Django raises NotSupportedError, which is a DatabaseError, so the view would catch it and tell every person on every submission that nothing was recorded.
findings.evidence: plan.md:79-88 and research.md:38-39 ('Nothing in the package listens for one' covers the package only). .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/django/db/models/query.py:845 (no signals) and 787-791 (NotSupportedError). .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/django/db/backends/oracle/features.py:69 supports_ignore_conflicts = False. Probed: issubclass(NotSupportedError, DatabaseError) is True. plan.md:108-110 catches DatabaseError. record() works on every backend through get_or_create (models.py:912-920).
findings.suggested_fix: Widen T003's documentation clause by two sentences in docs/models.md: record_many() sends no save signals where record() does, and it needs a database that supports ignoring conflicts, which rules out Oracle. No code and no test.

findings.claim: [architecture] get_destination() rebuilds a helper django-mvp already ships. NextURLMixin.get_next_url() reads next from the form on a POST and from the query string on a GET, checks it with url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme against the request's host, passes require_https, and refuses a bare word. The plan's version omits require_https, so on an https site a next of http://the-same-host/ is followed.
findings.evidence: plan.md:116-119. .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/mvp/views/edit.py:29-94, named as an available mixin at .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/mvp/views/__init__.py:18-22. Probed: url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme('http://testserver/x', {'testserver'}) is True, and False with require_https=True. Django's sign-in passes require_https=request.is_secure() at .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/django/contrib/auth/views.py:54-58.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add NextURLMixin to AgreementView's bases and have get_destination() start from self.get_next_url(), then apply the page's-own-address rule and the default; or keep the plan's own check and add require_https=self.request.is_secure() to it. The first removes code. One difference to accept with it: on a POST the mixin does not fall back to the query string, which the form's hidden field makes moot.

findings.claim: [architecture] T014 documents is_optional() as a method a project's own view can override. D16 says the method is a stand-in whose body #87 replaces. Publishing it as a supported override makes a public promise out of the stand-in: a project that overrides it sends people on with documents still outstanding, and #87 then has to keep or break that override.
findings.evidence: tasks.md:53 (T014: 'the two methods a project's own view can override') and plan.md:160-161. decisions.md D16: 'Revisit if: the site-wide check lands. Its answer replaces the method's body.' spec.md:402-404: 'Until then all outstanding documents are treated alike.'
findings.suggested_fix: In T014 and plan.md:160-161, document record_agreed() only as an override point. Leave is_optional() to its docstring, which says it answers False until the site-wide check decides. One clause removed from a docs task.

notes: agreement.js:2-3 says 'The server refuses a submission that leaves a required document unagreed'; the plan records what was agreed and shows the page again (FR-012). The script is frozen, so the wording stays until it is next touched.
research.md:27-28 and plan.md:183 count record() at three queries; on a new record it is two notice checks (models.py:902 and 1060), a read and a write, inside a savepoint.

research.md:43 'One bulk_create is one statement' holds up to the backend's batch size (about 199 rows of five fields on SQLite). Past that the view's transaction.atomic() is what keeps FR-010, so it is not only a precaution.

research.md:33 'on SQLite and PostgreSQL alike': the suite and CI run SQLite only. PostgreSQL's ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING is at django/db/backends/postgresql/operations.py:377-379 and is not exercised here.

plan.md:97: outstanding_for() already filters on a current version (models.py:114) and in_force() filters again (models.py:86), so the query joins versions twice. Harmless: one current version per document is a constraint. Probed: 2 queries, no duplicate rows.
CONTEXT.md:103-106 has Enforcement; the page says required and optional (D15). The Outstanding entry T014 writes is the place to say how the page's two words relate to enforced.
Watch item for T005: match the submitted 'agree' values as strings against the entries' version ids. Passing them to an ORM filter would raise ValueError on a non-numeric value and answer 500.
Watch item for T008: the except for DatabaseError and RecordError sits outside the transaction.atomic() block, not inside it. T007's scenario 4 test fails if it is inside.
Watch item for T003: derive the subject with Acceptance.subject_of(user), the single place it is derived (models.py:1004-1028).
The schema allows one top-level lens. It is set to spec-compliance; the three lenses are told apart by finding id prefix and by the bracketed tag opening each claim.
